title: 🕵️ The Sable Mirror
description: A state-heavy noir detective mystery with clue tracking, suspect trust, hidden evidence, pressure, gated interrogations, and conditional final accusations.

conditions.perfectCase: canAccuseHale() && canClearClara() && bellConfession && miraDraft && canMapCourier() && wrongAccusations == 0 && publicTrust >= 3 && timeLeft >= 4

nodes.label: Rain Summons
text: Rain polishes Sable Harbor until every streetlight looks guilty. The call comes at 2:13 a.m.: Lys Rowe, illusionist and civic darling, dead inside the locked observatory of the Glasswater Hotel.
Your partner, Finch, meets you under the awning with a soaked notebook. "The room was locked from inside, Mara. The mayor wants a name before breakfast."

nodes.label: First Look
nodes.text: The penthouse smells of champagne, lamp oil, and burned roses. A black mirror on the north wall carries a smeared message: THE CITY SAW.

nodes.label: Room Geometry
nodes.text: You mark the observatory: locked door, mirror wall, skylight, service bell, and a carpet dry under the body but damp under the window. Someone understood the room better than its guests.

nodes.label: Clock Photograph
nodes.text: The flash catches the mantle clock at 1:47, its glass cracked in a star. The police photographer grumbles, but the image preserves a minute nobody has explained. 📷

nodes.label: Lobby Whispers
nodes.text: The night concierge gives you the guest list and three useful lies: no one used the service lift, no one heard a singer crying, and no one knows why a rose box is missing.

nodes.label: Black Mirror
nodes.text: Lys lies beside the mirror wall, one glove missing. Rain ticks on the skylight. Finch waits for your first theory, but the room resists simple answers.

nodes.label: Mirror Words
nodes.text: The words were written with soot and stage grease. The final stroke slants upward, as if Lys wrote while looking at someone reflected behind her.

nodes.label: Quiet Pulse
nodes.text: No blood. No bruise worth the city coroner's ink. But her lips hold a bitter almond ghost beneath the cosmetic wax. Poison, then theater, then locked-room theater.

nodes.label: Case Board
text: Finch pins your evidence to a portable board. {{hasClockPhoto:The clock photo sits under the mirror message. }}{{hasBlueThread:A blue thread curls beside the guest list. }}{{hasLedgerPage:A ledger page waits like a loaded pistol. }}
Your current focus: {{suspectFocus:Clara Voss.|Silas Hale.|Mira Quill.|Orson Bell.|Ilya Rook.}} The rain keeps time against the windows.

nodes.label: Hotel Return
nodes.text: The Glasswater Hotel has stopped pretending to sleep. Staff polish empty glasses while reporters crowd the velvet ropes outside.

nodes.label: Penthouse Again
nodes.text: Without the first rush of uniforms, the observatory becomes quieter and stranger. Dust has gathered where shoes should have disturbed it.

nodes.label: Glass Floor
nodes.text: Three details wait in the locked room. None shouts. That usually means all three matter.

nodes.label: Ash Trace
nodes.text: The ash tray holds rose-stem ash and a glittering dust that clings to your glove. Stage powder, expensive and faintly medicinal.

nodes.label: Blue Thread
nodes.text: A blue silk thread snags on the brass latch of the mirror wall. Clara Voss wore blue on stage tonight, but so did half the hotel orchestra.

nodes.label: Candle Timing
nodes.text: The candle beside Lys burned unevenly. Someone trimmed it after death, staging a later time and trusting smoke to make you lazy.

nodes.label: Penthouse Closed
nodes.text: You seal the room with three notes circled: powder, silk, false time. Finch looks at the mirror wall and says, "That wall wants to be a door."

nodes.label: Powder Bloom
nodes.text: Under a lamp, the dust blooms green at the edge. Not cyanide itself, but a binder used in stage cosmetic. Lys wore it. Someone handled it.

nodes.label: Thread Ledger
nodes.text: The thread has wax on it, not perfume. It came from a costume stored near candles, not necessarily from Clara's dress.

nodes.label: False Minute
nodes.text: You compare the candle gutter with the photographed clock. Death came closer to 1:31 than 1:47. Fifteen minutes have gone missing.

nodes.label: Staff Ledger
nodes.text: The staff ledger sits behind the reception cage, written in three inks and one nervous hand. The night clerk claims the gaps are normal.

nodes.label: Lobby Names
nodes.text: Names, keys, and excuses crowd the page. The clerk watches which line your finger chooses.

nodes.label: Concierge Nerves
nodes.text: The concierge admits Clara came through the lobby after one, eyes bright with rain or tears. He omitted it because Mr. Hale dislikes scandal before breakfast.

nodes.label: Torn Stub
nodes.text: From his wastebasket, you recover a torn cloakroom stub marked with the theater's midnight seal. It smells of burned paper.

nodes.label: Night Clerk
nodes.text: The clerk finally shows the late key log. Orson Bell signed out a maintenance ring at 12:58 and returned it with one brass tag polished clean.

nodes.label: Polished Tag
nodes.text: Fresh polish hides fingerprints but not impatience. The clerk says Orson looked frightened, not proud.

nodes.label: Room Cards
nodes.text: One room card has been filed under the wrong suite. The number belongs to Lys, but the ink matches Hale's private office stationery.

nodes.label: Card Gamble
nodes.text: You dust the card while the desk fan rattles. A print may be there, if the cheap powder cooperates.

nodes.label: Partial Print
nodes.text: The print is partial but useful: a square ring, city council crest, worn on Hale's right hand in every newspaper photograph.

nodes.label: List Complete
nodes.text: The staff ledger gives you three doors into the case: Clara's hidden lobby passage, Orson's maintenance ring, and Hale's impossible room card.

nodes.label: Service Hall
nodes.text: Behind the velvet lobby, the hotel becomes pipes, wet stone, and low electric hum. A service lift waits under a sign reading STAFF ONLY.

nodes.label: Hidden Routes
nodes.text: The service hall offers three ways to make a locked room stop looking magical.

nodes.label: Lift Cage
nodes.text: The lift stops between floors where hotel blueprints pretend there is only wall. Someone used the old illusion corridor.

nodes.label: Reflection Slot
nodes.text: A narrow slot lets a person see the observatory through angled glass. The victim could have seen the killer without facing them.

nodes.label: Mirror Seam
nodes.text: The mirror wall opens with a sigh when you press a screw hidden under silver leaf. Orson told uniforms it was fixed shut.

nodes.label: Dust Fall
nodes.text: Dust falls from the seam. Finch catches a metal glint before it drops into the grate.

nodes.label: Roof Hatch
nodes.text: On the roof, a janitor smoking under the rain tank admits he saw a courier cross from the river stairs carrying white roses.

nodes.label: Rooftop Name
nodes.text: The janitor knows the courier only as Rook. He says Rook limped after leaving, as if one shoe hid something hard.

nodes.label: Hall Complete
nodes.text: The hotel route is no miracle: service lift, mirror seam, roof hatch. The question is who had courage, key, and reason.

nodes.label: Hotel Pattern
nodes.text: By dawn the Glasswater has given up its architecture. Finch writes ACCESS IS A CONSPIRACY across the top of the board.

nodes.label: Stage Circuit
nodes.text: The theater district wakes late and lies early. Lys rehearsed here, Clara sang here, and Mira Quill bought drinks here for anyone with a secret.

nodes.label: Dressing Room
nodes.text: Lys's dressing room has been searched badly. Drawers gape open, but the makeup mirror still hides a strip of paper under its frame.

nodes.label: Backstage Clues
nodes.text: Backstage dust records panic in smaller handwriting than people do.

nodes.label: Farewell Strip
nodes.text: The paper is a letter in Clara's hand: not a threat, a farewell. "I will not be your alibi anymore," it says.

nodes.label: Not Motive
nodes.text: The letter bruises Clara, but it does not convict her. It places her hurt before midnight, not at the mirror wall.

nodes.label: Makeup Tray
nodes.text: One stage vial is missing from the tray. Its label says pearl base, but the residue smells like almonds under the greasepaint.

nodes.label: Cosmetic Poison
nodes.text: A dresser remembers Mira borrowing the tray to "test a column detail." A journalist with stage poison is either brilliant or terrified.

nodes.label: Clara Song
nodes.text: Clara sings one line before answering: "Lys was alive when I left." The tremor in her voice arrives on alive, not left.

nodes.label: Stage Door
nodes.text: The stage doorman confirms Clara left at 1:22 by the alley, before your corrected time of death. Her lie protects grief, not opportunity.

nodes.label: Room Cleared
nodes.text: The dressing room clears one suspect without clearing the night. Clara had motive to cry, not a route to kill.

nodes.label: News Desk
nodes.text: Mira Quill's newspaper office smells of ink and sleeplessness. Her desk is empty except for a typewriter ribbon left warm under its cover.

nodes.label: Column Draft
nodes.text: A locked drawer, a trash basket, and a wall of clipped scandals compete for your attention.

nodes.label: Ribbon Ghost
nodes.text: You shade the ribbon against a lamp. The last column named Hale's debt, Bell's key work, and Lys as the source.

nodes.label: Missing Ending
nodes.text: The final paragraph is ripped from the ribbon record. Mira found the truth and then removed the route.

nodes.label: Trash Basket
nodes.text: A burned note survives in the metal basket: Pay the mirror man or I print the ledger. The signature is only an initial, L.

nodes.label: Blackmail Shape
nodes.text: Lys was blackmailing someone with access to an engineer and fear of print. That narrows the city more than politics likes.

nodes.label: Scandal Wall
nodes.text: Mira's wall links Hale to river bonds, Orson to hotel renovations, and Ilya Rook to sealed courier deliveries.

nodes.label: Reporter Fear
nodes.text: A note in Mira's shorthand says, "If I disappear, ask why the roses came from the river." She expected danger and kept writing.

nodes.label: Desk Closed
nodes.text: Mira's desk gives you motive, warning, and a missing paragraph. She hid the route, not the murder.

nodes.label: Gala Circle
nodes.text: The gala survivors occupy a private club where everyone speaks softly because every table has a reporter under it.

nodes.label: Witness Drift
nodes.text: Three witnesses remember the same hour differently, which means one remembers it usefully.

nodes.label: Mayor Smile
nodes.text: The mayor calls Hale "indispensable" twice. That is not praise. It is fear wearing dinner clothes.

nodes.label: Political Risk
nodes.text: Pushing the mayor may earn a clearer answer or a louder complaint.

nodes.label: Violinist
nodes.text: The violinist saw Lys argue with a man in engineer gray, then burn a theater ticket in a candle flame.

nodes.label: Grey Sleeve
nodes.text: The sleeve was hotel gray, but the cufflink was council silver. Someone dressed one class down to move unseen.

nodes.label: Coat Girl
nodes.text: The coat girl handled a white rose box that nobody claimed. It was heavy, damp, and addressed to Lys in block letters.

nodes.label: Rose Memory
nodes.text: She can almost remember the courier's face. Fear makes memory slippery.

nodes.label: Courier Scar
nodes.text: She remembers a crescent scar at the courier's jaw and a limp after he left. Rook becomes less rumor and more address.

nodes.label: Circle Broken
nodes.text: The gala witnesses give you political fear, a burned ticket, and a rose box. Everyone saw something. Nobody wanted to be first.

nodes.label: Theater Pattern
nodes.text: The theater district clears Clara's timeline and turns Mira's draft into a loaded question. Finch writes ROSES FROM RIVER beside the mirror sketch.

nodes.label: River Work
nodes.text: The river district smells of diesel, wet rope, and fish market coffee. If the rose box came through here, it left a wake.

nodes.label: Cold Room
nodes.text: The coroner has Lys under a sheet and two cups of coffee under his belt. "Not a romantic death," he says. "Those are rarely so tidy."

nodes.label: Medical Clues
nodes.text: The body has three stories left, if you ask carefully.

nodes.label: Toxin Test
nodes.text: The coroner's reagent turns violet in the cosmetic residue. The poison rode in makeup wax, not wine.

nodes.label: Wax Carrier
nodes.text: That delivery method required someone who knew Lys would touch her face before stepping into the mirror room.

nodes.label: Broken Watch
nodes.text: Lys's wristwatch stopped at 1:32, crushed when she fell. It agrees with your candle correction and humiliates the staged clock.

nodes.label: Minute Anchor
nodes.text: The missing fifteen minutes become a corridor: enough time to enter, poison, speak, leave, and stage the room.

nodes.label: Missing Glove
nodes.text: The missing glove was cut from Lys's right hand after death. Someone removed powder transfer before uniforms arrived.

nodes.label: Late Cleanup
nodes.text: Cleanup means panic or planning. Either way, the killer expected the police to look at doors before skin.

nodes.label: Morgue Closed
nodes.text: The medical facts are simple enough to be cruel: poison, false time, removed glove. The locked room was a stage after the murder.

nodes.label: Courier Shed
nodes.text: Rook's shed stands behind a shuttered fishmonger. A white rose petal floats in an oil puddle by the door.

nodes.label: Rook Shed
nodes.text: Ilya Rook is absent. His shed offers a ledger, a boot rack, and a locked ice chest.

nodes.label: Delivery Book
nodes.text: The book records a rose box to Lys, paid by S.H. and routed through an old hotel service stair.

nodes.label: Initials Burn
nodes.text: The initials are too neat. Hale wanted deniability, not invisibility. That usually means he trusted another person to finish the dirty work.

nodes.label: Boot Rack
nodes.text: One boot hides a brass splinter in the heel. It matches the mirror seam, explaining Rook's limp after the gala.

nodes.label: Reluctant Courier
nodes.text: Rook crossed the roof and touched the mirror seam, but a courier's route is not the same as a killer's hand.

nodes.label: Ice Chest
nodes.text: The chest contains wilted white roses and a false bottom lined with waxed cloth. The poison vial was not stored here, only transported.

nodes.label: Hidden Label
nodes.text: A soaked label clings to the false bottom. It might lift cleanly or dissolve under your tweezers.

nodes.label: Wax Label
nodes.text: The label shows the hotel florist did not pack the box. It came from Hale's campaign warehouse by the river.

nodes.label: Shed Closed
nodes.text: Rook delivered access in a rose box. Whether he knew it carried murder is still open, but his route ties river to mirror.

nodes.label: Tail Route
nodes.text: Finch finds Rook drinking tea behind a ferry office. He runs when he sees your badge, which is either guilt or excellent survival.

nodes.label: Rain Chase
nodes.text: You chase him through fish stalls and under steam pipes. The wet stones choose sides at random.

nodes.label: Rook Caught
nodes.text: You corner Rook under the ferry clock. He raises both hands and says, "I delivered a box, detective. I did not know it held a door."

nodes.label: Courier Confession
nodes.text: Rook names Orson as the man who showed him where to leave the box, and Hale as the man whose envelope paid twice the normal rate.

nodes.label: Lost Corner
nodes.text: Rook vanishes behind a tram. You find only a torn delivery receipt and your own temper steaming in the rain.

nodes.label: Receipt Mark
nodes.text: The receipt still carries a hotel service mark and Hale's campaign warehouse code. Missing the man does not erase the route.

nodes.label: Public Scene
nodes.text: A patrol wagon cuts off the wrong alley. Reporters see you shove through a crowd, and the morning edition will not be kind.

nodes.label: Witness Slip
nodes.text: A ferry clerk quietly hands Finch a note after the scene: Rook was frightened of Orson Bell, not Lys Rowe.

nodes.label: Route Marked
nodes.text: Whatever the chase cost, the river now points at the hotel corridor. The rose box carried access, not romance.

nodes.label: Dock Pattern
nodes.text: The docks give you poison delivery, missing time, and Rook's service route. Finch draws a red line from river warehouse to mirror seam.

nodes.label: Paper City
nodes.text: Sable Harbor keeps its real sins in ledgers, permits, and basement plans. Paper does not confess, but it tears under pressure.

nodes.label: City Archive
nodes.text: The city archive has the temperature of a tomb and the manners of a bank. A clerk tries to send you away with a form for a form.

nodes.label: Archive Search
nodes.text: You can search permits, renovation plans, or old fire maps before the clerk's patience expires.

nodes.label: Permit Stack
nodes.text: The permit stack is misfiled, naturally. You can charm the clerk or start moving boxes.

nodes.label: Ledger Page
nodes.text: Inside a permit folder, you find a copied ledger page listing Hale's river bond debt and payments to Bell Maintenance.

nodes.label: Renovation Plans
nodes.text: The renovation plan labels the mirror corridor as decorative glasswork. Someone paid extra to misname a passage.

nodes.label: Hidden Passage
nodes.text: A pencil note names Orson Bell as consulting engineer and Silas Hale as sponsor. The city signed off without inspection.

nodes.label: Fire Maps
nodes.text: Old fire maps show the roof hatch once fed an escape stair. Bell's later plan bricked it into a one-person corridor.

nodes.label: Escape Ghost
nodes.text: The map makes Rook's route practical and the locked room fraudulent. Architecture, once paid, becomes testimony.

nodes.label: Archive Closed
nodes.text: The archive yields motive, access, and official negligence. The clerk asks if you found what you needed. Finch says, "We found what they needed hidden."

nodes.label: Bell Shop
nodes.text: Orson Bell's workshop is under the hotel laundry. Tools hang in exact rows, the kind of order that hides panic well.

nodes.label: Engineer Bench
nodes.text: A workbench, a key mold, and an invoice spike wait under the humming bulb.

nodes.label: Fresh Filing
nodes.text: Metal filings on the bench match the mirror seam screw. Bell worked on the passage after claiming it had been sealed for months.

nodes.label: Engineer Lie
nodes.text: A careful lie is still a door. Bell may not have killed Lys, but he made the room possible.

nodes.label: Key Mold
nodes.text: The key mold holds brass dust from a duplicate service key. The shape matches the polished tag from the hotel desk.

nodes.label: Duplicate Route
nodes.text: The duplicate would open the service corridor, not the public door. That explains the locked-room trick without touching the impossible.

nodes.label: Invoice Spike
nodes.text: Three invoices from Bell Maintenance were paid by Hale's campaign fund. The last is marked mirror adjustment, urgent.

nodes.label: Bell Pressure
nodes.text: Bell returns early and sees you at the invoice spike. His face folds before his mouth lies.

nodes.label: Bell Cracks
nodes.text: Bell admits he sold access and made a duplicate key. He swears Hale ordered the passage opened and Rook delivered the box.

nodes.label: Shop Closed
nodes.text: Bell's workshop turns the mirror from miracle into mechanism. Hale bought the mechanism, Bell built it, and Rook carried it.

nodes.label: Bank Files
nodes.text: The bank manager hates subpoenas almost as much as he hates wet detectives on marble floors.

nodes.label: Debt Trail
nodes.text: The files can show Hale's debt, Mira's payments, or campaign warehouse rentals.

nodes.label: Debt Note
nodes.text: Hale owed river bonds to men who break fingers for punctuation. Lys's ledger could have ended his career and his breathing.

nodes.label: Pressure Math
nodes.text: Debt plus blackmail is motive. Debt plus a mirror corridor is a plan trying to look clever.

nodes.label: Mira Payment
nodes.text: Mira paid for copies of Hale's debt statements three days before the gala. Her column was a fuse, not a confession.

nodes.label: Reporter Trail
nodes.text: She followed money to Lys and then to Bell. If she hid anything, it was the source she feared would be killed next.

nodes.label: Warehouse Rent
nodes.text: The campaign rented a river warehouse under a civic charity name. White rose boxes shipped from it on gala night.

nodes.label: Charity Mask
nodes.text: Hale laundered logistics through charity paperwork. Sable Harbor does love a sin with letterhead.

nodes.label: Bank Closed
nodes.text: The bank files finish the money trail: debt, reporter pressure, warehouse route. The case now has a skeleton.

nodes.label: Paper Pattern
nodes.text: Records turn suspicion into structure. Finch pins debt, access, warehouse, and mirror plan into one ugly rectangle.

nodes.label: Interview Hall
nodes.text: You borrow a municipal hearing room. Five suspects wait outside in five different kinds of silence.

nodes.label: Clara Waits
nodes.text: Clara Voss keeps her gloves folded in her lap. The blue silk thread on your board has made her old grief look like evidence.

nodes.label: Clara Questions
nodes.text: Clara will answer more if you show her you know the difference between grief and murder.

nodes.label: Letter Mercy
nodes.text: Clara cries when you place the farewell letter between you. "I lied because the last thing I said to her was cruel."

nodes.label: Clock Truth
nodes.text: The watch and photograph let Clara fix her timeline. She left before the true death window, then returned to the lobby too late.

nodes.label: Thread Hurt
nodes.text: She recognizes the waxed thread as costume repair silk from the theater, used by three stagehands and one nervous illusionist.

nodes.label: Clara Cleared
nodes.text: You let Clara leave through the side door. Clearing one suspect does not make the room cleaner, but it makes the case more honest.

nodes.label: Hale Arrives
nodes.text: Silas Hale enters with a lawyer, a carnation, and the bright anger of a man unused to narrow rooms.

nodes.label: Hale Questions
nodes.text: Hale smiles at weak evidence and sweats at documents. Choose which kind of truth to bring.

nodes.label: Debt Flinch
nodes.text: The ledger page makes Hale touch his ring. "Forgery," he says, before reading enough to know what it says.

nodes.label: Rose Pressure
nodes.text: You ask why his campaign warehouse shipped roses to a dead woman. His lawyer reaches for the door.

nodes.label: Ring Print
nodes.text: When you mention the partial ring print, Hale stops smiling at the wrong half-second. The lawyer notices too.

nodes.label: Hale Sweats
nodes.text: Hale leaves without confessing, but his timeline now has a crack: he denies the room card before you mention which card.

nodes.label: Mira Arrives
nodes.text: Mira Quill brings her own notebook to interrogation, which is either arrogance or habit. Possibly both.

nodes.label: Mira Questions
nodes.text: Mira respects clean questions and despises moral theater. That makes her useful if you can resist performing.

nodes.label: Column Source
nodes.text: Mira admits Lys was her source. "She wanted Hale exposed, not dead. I cut the route because Rook begged me."

nodes.label: Poison Denial
nodes.text: Mira borrowed the makeup tray to prove poison access, then returned it. Her mistake made her look useful to a killer.

nodes.label: Roses Note
nodes.text: She gives you the missing paragraph: "The roses came through Hale's charity warehouse and Bell's corridor."

nodes.label: Mira Released
nodes.text: Mira leaves you one sentence for free: "If Hale falls alone, the city will pretend Bell was a tool, not a door."

nodes.label: Orson Waits
nodes.text: Orson Bell sits with his hands flat on the table, as if hiding the memory of every key he has ever copied.

nodes.label: Orson Questions
nodes.text: Bell can be broken by mechanism, money, or fear. Pick the tool carefully.

nodes.label: Mechanism Trap
nodes.text: You describe the seam screw by screw. Bell corrects one detail before realizing he has corrected a confession.

nodes.label: Invoice Trap
nodes.text: Bell whispers, "Hale said it was leverage, not murder." Then he asks if accessory is spelled with one c or two.

nodes.label: Courier Trap
nodes.text: Rook's name makes Bell fold. He confirms the rose box hid a duplicate key and a route note.

nodes.label: Bell Held
nodes.text: You hold Bell as an accessory. He looks relieved, which tells you he expected Hale to arrange worse.

nodes.label: Ilya Waits
nodes.text: Ilya Rook sits nearest the exit. Couriers measure rooms by escape routes first and furniture second.

nodes.label: Ilya Questions
nodes.text: Rook needs proof that you know the route and mercy enough not to confuse courier with author.

nodes.label: Box Mercy
nodes.text: Rook says the box was sealed by Bell, paid by Hale, and too heavy for roses. He thought it carried documents.

nodes.label: Route Mercy
nodes.text: When you draw the service corridor, Rook marks the missing minute: Bell took the box from him at the roof hatch.

nodes.label: Voices Sorted
nodes.text: Five interviews leave one pattern: Clara grieved, Mira chased, Rook carried, Bell opened, Hale paid. The verb that matters is still killed.

nodes.label: Rebuild Night
nodes.text: The board is dense enough to become weather. You need turn evidence into sequence before City Hall turns sequence into fog.

nodes.label: Timeline Board
nodes.text: You pin the corrected death window beside the broken watch and clock photograph. The false 1:47 collapses.

nodes.label: Minute Chain
nodes.text: The missing minutes need a human shape.

nodes.label: Clara Gap
nodes.text: Clara's return came after the true window. You write CLEAR by her name, and the board breathes.

nodes.label: Rook Gap
nodes.text: Rook's missing minute belongs to Bell taking the rose box. The courier carried the door, then lost control of it.

nodes.label: Poison Board
nodes.text: You align the vial, powder trace, missing glove, and cosmetic wax. The poison story stops wobbling.

nodes.label: Toxin Chain
nodes.text: The toxin needs a carrier and a hand.

nodes.label: Carrier Fixed
nodes.text: The makeup wax delivered poison before Lys entered the mirror room. Whoever planned it knew her stage habits.

nodes.label: Cleanup Fixed
nodes.text: The missing glove proves the killer or helper returned after collapse. That points away from sudden passion and toward staging.

nodes.label: Route Board
nodes.text: You layer the hotel plan over Rook's delivery route. River, roof hatch, service corridor, mirror seam: the impossible becomes a hallway.

nodes.label: Access Chain
nodes.text: The hallway needs keys.

nodes.label: Key Fixed
nodes.text: The duplicate key puts the corridor under human control. Locks are honest only when keys are honest.

nodes.label: Bell Fixed
nodes.text: Bell's access proof lets you charge him without letting Hale hide behind him.

nodes.label: Motive Board
nodes.text: Debt, blackmail, and a newspaper fuse form a motive ugly enough for City Hall.

nodes.label: Motive Chain
nodes.text: You test whether the motive belongs to Hale alone or to the people orbiting him.

nodes.label: Hale Motive
nodes.text: Hale had the debt, the public office, and the money trail. His motive is not emotional. It is administrative.

nodes.label: Mira Motive
nodes.text: Mira had fear and access to information, but the money never bends toward her. She held a match, not the fuse.

nodes.label: Bell Motive
nodes.text: Bell had access and fear, but every payment chain points upward. A paid door is not the hand that orders it opened.

nodes.label: Theory Locks
nodes.text: The board resolves: Hale paid, Bell opened, Rook carried, Mira nearly printed, Clara mourned, Lys saw too much.

nodes.label: Last Walk
nodes.text: Finch buttons his coat. "We can take this upstairs now. Question is whether upstairs wants truth or a suspect."

nodes.label: Accusation Room
nodes.text: The prosecutor gives you one hearing before the city wakes. Your accusation must carry motive, access, poison, and sequence.

nodes.label: Hale Named
nodes.text: You name Silas Hale. The room tightens. Hale laughs once, too loud, and the prosecutor looks down at the ledger page before looking at you.

nodes.label: Verdict Weight
nodes.text: Your file lands on the table. The city weighs whether to sacrifice one man or expose its own machinery.

nodes.label: Narrow File
nodes.text: The file is strong enough to indict Hale, but not clean enough to pull every accomplice into daylight. The prosecutor chooses the charge he can win.

nodes.label: Clara Named
nodes.text: Clara's blue thread looks dramatic on the table. Then the corrected timeline, farewell letter, and watch make drama look cheap.

nodes.label: Thread Snaps
nodes.text: The room waits to see whether you can recover from accusing grief itself.

nodes.label: Bell Named
nodes.text: Bell wilts under the accusation, but his confession keeps pointing upward. He built the door. He did not choose the death.

nodes.label: Accessory Pivot
nodes.text: If your Hale file is strong, Bell's fear may become a bridge. If not, it becomes a scapegoat.

nodes.label: Mira Named
nodes.text: Mira watches you accuse her with the exhausted disappointment of a woman who already wrote the better ending.

nodes.label: Column Burns
nodes.text: Her draft explains too much to make her the killer. The prosecutor sees it before you finish.

nodes.label: Ilya Named
nodes.text: Rook does not defend himself well. Couriers are trained to run, not speak. But the route proves a delivery, not intent.

nodes.label: Courier Breaks
nodes.text: Rook's statement either helps you pivot to Hale or collapses under the weight of your mistake.

nodes.label: Weak Theory
nodes.text: You bring the case upstairs before the board has hardened. The prosecutor listens because the city is watching, not because the file is ready.

nodes.label: Thin File
nodes.text: A thin case can still cut, but it usually cuts the hand holding it.

nodes.label: Mirror Ledger
nodes.text: Bell signs, Rook confirms, Mira prints, and Clara's timeline holds. Hale's lawyer asks for a recess. The city hears the mirror answer first.

nodes.label: Case Cold
nodes.text: By sunrise, the prosecutor closes the file as a tragic poisoning by unknown hand. The Glasswater reopens within a week. Every mirror in the lobby looks away.

nodes.label: Badge Surrendered
nodes.text: Heat swallows the case. City Hall removes you for misconduct, Hale praises due process, and the evidence room loses one box with your name on it.

nodes.label: Burnout
nodes.text: You push past the edge of focus and the case becomes noise: rain, ink, voices, mirrors. Finch takes you home before the city takes your badge.

nodes.label: Wrong Accusation
nodes.text: Your accusation lands on the wrong life. The real machinery keeps turning, cleaner now because you taught it where the weak parts were.

nodes.label: Narrow Conviction
nodes.text: Hale is indicted for Lys Rowe's murder. Bell takes an accessory charge, Rook survives as witness, and the city pretends the mirror was only one man's crime.

nodes.label: Perfect Case
nodes.text: The full file breaks open: Hale, Bell, the warehouse, the corridor, the poison, and the cover-up. Lys Rowe gets the truth she wrote for, and Sable Harbor has to look into its own mirror.
